landing.heroTitle: Type one word you still remember.
landing.heroSub: Wi-fi passwords, router configs, contract numbers, warranty codes. Save them under the keyword you will think of, not in a folder you will never open again.
landing.demoCaption: Sample data — type freely, nothing is sent anywhere.
landing.explainMatchBody: Names that start with what you type come first. Wrong accents, missing accents and partial words still find it.
landing.explainNearBody: In the app, they get their own group below. Turning the group on or off never reshuffles the order you are used to.
landing.explainSaveBody: In the app, type wifi #home: content and press Enter. No other screen to open.
landing.wallSub: Small things, needed often, always filed somewhere you can't recall.
landing.jsonTitle: Paste JSON, read it as a table
landing.jsonBody: Router config, API responses, exports — paste them as-is. Nested objects open level by level, arrays become tables with columns.
landing.jsonNote: Edit one cell and only that cell changes. A long number like 9007199254740993 keeps every digit; nothing is rounded behind your back.
landing.privacyTitle: Plainly: what is encrypted and what is not
landing.privacyBody1: Entry content will be locked in your browser with a key only your machine holds. We keep no copy and have no way to read it.
landing.privacyBody2: Item names and tags are not encrypted — they are what makes search work. If you turn on similar-meaning search, those two are sent to an embedding server we run ourselves. Entry content never is, even then.
landing.encBody: The content of every text and json entry.
landing.plainBody: Item names, tag names, edit times, entry counts.
landing.cryptoNote: XChaCha20-Poly1305 · Argon2id · keys never leave the browser
landing.recoveryTitle: Forgetting your passphrase is not losing everything
landing.recoveryBody: Because we do not hold your key, you need your own way back. There are three, set up at sign-up.
landing.recoveryKeysBody: Print them, put them away. Each one opens the vault on its own, once.
landing.recoveryPasskeyBody: Fingerprint or security key. Open the vault without typing anything.
landing.recoveryDeviceBody: Your usual machine opens straight away; an unfamiliar one does not.
landing.ctaBody: Free, no cap on items. Needs an email and a passphrase you use nowhere else.

legal.title: Terms of Service & Privacy Policy
legal.lead: Short, plain-language Terms of Service and Privacy Policy aligned with engram’s encryption model: end-to-end encrypted entry bodies, plaintext item names/tags/hints/search queries for search, no selling of data, export and account deletion status, and contact channels.

terms.heading: Terms of Service
terms.s1Body: engram stores keyword-indexed text notes and structured json tables. Your account login password (or linked Google/GitHub OAuth account) authenticates your session with the server. Your vault passphrase is completely separate and locks your entry contents. Resetting your login password by email restores account access only and never unlocks or decrypts your vault.
terms.s2Title: 1.2 · Your responsibility for keys and recovery
terms.s2Body: The server stores only ciphertext and wrapped keys and holds no decryption key, so we cannot decrypt or recover your entries for you. This protection assumes the app code delivered to your browser is not tampered with (see the threat model in the technical documentation). At vault setup you must save your 10 single-use recovery keys (and may add a passkey or a remembered device). If all unlock paths and decryptable backups are lost, the only option is a vault reset, which permanently deletes encrypted entry bodies on the server while keeping item names and tags.
terms.s3Title: 1.3 · Data ownership and acceptable use limits
terms.s3Body: You retain full ownership of the data you store. Do not use the service to store unlawful content, distribute malware, or disrupt system availability. Each entry is capped at 256 KiB, with up to 200 entries and 20 tags per item to keep sync reliable.

privacy.heading: Privacy Policy & End-to-End Scope
privacy.intro: Plainly: what is end-to-end encrypted in your browser and what is stored as plaintext on the server.
privacy.encBody: The body of every text and json entry is encrypted in your browser (XChaCha20-Poly1305, key derived via Argon2id 64 MiB in a Web Worker). The server stores only ciphertext and wrapped keys and has no decryption key. This protection assumes the app code delivered to your browser is not tampered with (see the threat model in the technical documentation).
privacy.plainBody: Item names (name), tags (tag), hints (hint), and the text you search are NOT encrypted so keyword search and suggestions work. The server also sees entry type, timestamps, counts, and can infer plaintext length from ciphertext size. Never put passwords or secrets in item names, tags, or hints.
privacy.tableAriaLabel: Data encryption and server visibility summary
privacy.row3Purpose: Seen by server for search; when semantic suggest (≈, arrives with the upcoming search release) is on, may be sent to an embedding provider, which can be a third-party service
privacy.row4Data: Email, settings, sessions, security audit log
privacy.row4Purpose: Account authentication & security audit; login passwords hashed with Argon2id
privacy.s21Title: 2.1 · Semantic suggest (arrives with the upcoming search release) & access logs
privacy.s21Body: When optional semantic suggest (≈, arrives with the upcoming search release) is enabled, item names, tags, hints, and the text you search may be sent to an embedding provider, which can be a third-party service, to compute similarity vectors; entry bodies are never sent. Turning semantic suggest off in Settings stops sending data and deletes stored vectors. Server access logs do not record search queries and never record entry bodies, passphrases, or recovery keys.

deletion.heading: We Do Not Sell Data, Export & Account Deletion
deletion.noSellBody: We never sell, rent, or monetize your data for advertising. We use an HttpOnly sign-in session cookie, a JavaScript-readable anti-CSRF cookie, and two UI preference cookies (locale and light/dark theme) — no third-party advertising trackers.
deletion.exportDeleteBody: Self-serve data export and account deletion are being added (later release); until then request them through the contact channel below. When an account is deleted, its vault, wrapped recovery keys, passkeys, items, tags, and encrypted entries are removed from the live database; security audit logs are retained by default for 90 days, and database backups / PITR copies age out on their own schedule.

settings.title: Passkey
settings.body: Unlock your vault with biometrics or a security key. Your browser and authenticator must support vault unlock; we check this when you add a passkey.

onboarding.title: Add a passkey (optional)
onboarding.lead: Unlock your vault with fingerprint, face, or a security key instead of typing your passphrase every time. Skipping is fine — your passphrase and 10 recovery keys are already enough.
onboarding.cardBody: Requires a PRF-capable authenticator. We verify PRF support during registration; if unsupported, nothing is saved.
onboarding.reauthNote: Clicking Add passkey first asks you to confirm your account (login password or Google) before your browser shows the passkey prompt.

forgot.passkeyBody: Unlock with a registered passkey on the unlock screen, then go to Settings › Security to set a new passphrase without the old one.
forgot.deviceBody: Another browser or machine that remembers this vault may still open silently so you can set a new passphrase in Settings.
forgot.unlockedTabTitle: A tab that is still unlocked
forgot.unlockedTabBody: If another tab or device still has this vault unlocked, open Settings › Security › Change passphrase (no old passphrase needed).

passkeys.loadError: Could not load your registered passkeys.
passkeys.renameFailed: Could not rename this passkey. Try again.
passkeys.revokeDialogDescription: Re-authenticate your account to remove {name} from the server.
passkeys.revokeNotFoundError: Could not remove this passkey because it was not found on the server.
passkeys.revokeFailed: Could not remove this passkey. Try again.
passkeys.revokeNoteBody: (requires account re-auth) deletes this passkey and its protected copy of the vault key from the live server. It does not remove the passkey from your authenticator, and copies or backups made earlier can still be opened while your authenticator keeps this passkey.

autoLock.title: Auto-lock
autoLock.body: Locks the vault after inactivity across all tabs. Default is 15 minutes; press L to lock immediately.
autoLock.saveError: Could not save auto-lock setting. Reverted to the previous value.

unlock.recoveredNoticeBody: Your new passphrase was saved. Unlock your vault with the new passphrase.
unlock.title: Unlock vault
unlock.lead: Item names and tags remain searchable while locked. Entry contents need your decryption key, and only this browser can open it.
unlock.caption: Slow devices may take a few seconds. Key derivation runs entirely inside your browser.

errors.incorrectPassphraseBody: There is no hint and no remaining-attempts counter — verification happens locally on your device, and the server never knows your passphrase. Use a passkey, a remembered device, or a recovery key if needed.
errors.invalidUnicodeBody: Passphrase contains invalid Unicode characters. Re-type your vault passphrase.
errors.privateKeysWrapInvalidTitle: Could not verify vault key pair
errors.privateKeysWrapInvalidBody: The vault key opened, but another key stored with your vault could not be verified. This is not a wrong-passphrase error — reload and try again.
errors.oomTitle: Not enough memory to unlock your vault
errors.oomBodyPrefix: This browser could not set aside the 64 MiB of memory needed to derive the key from your passphrase.
errors.oomBodyStrong: This does not mean your passphrase is wrong.
errors.oomBodySuffix: Unlock with a passkey or remembered device, close other tabs, or try another device.
errors.busyBody: Another vault operation is currently running in this tab. Wait a moment for it to finish.
errors.recoveringTitle: Recovery is in progress in this tab
errors.recoveringBody: Finish setting a new passphrase on the recovery screen, or lock the vault first to switch back to normal unlock.
errors.sessionExpiredBody: Unlocking the vault requires an active sign-in session. Sign in again to return to this unlock screen.
errors.networkBody: Could not load your encrypted vault bundle. Check your connection and try again.

forgotPassphrase.title: Forgot passphrase
forgotPassphrase.lead: The server cannot read your entry contents, so there is no "reset passphrase by email" link. Instead, use one of the recovery paths you set up.

paths.recoveryKeyBody: Use one unused key from the 10-key set you saved when creating your vault.

reauthNote.title: Re-authenticate your account before entering a recovery key
reauthNote.body: Starting recovery asks you to confirm your account (login password or Google, valid for 5 minutes) before you paste your recovery key, so a sign-in redirect never clears the vault key you just opened.

lastResort.title: If every unlock path is gone: check your encrypted backups first.
lastResort.body: The final option is to reset your vault — permanently deleting all encrypted entry contents while keeping your item names and tags. Resetting only clears the live server; any backup files you hold are untouched.

recovery.invalid: That recovery key is not valid.
recovery.need_new_passphrase: Set a new passphrase to finish recovery.

step1.title: Confirm your account to start recovery
step1.lead: Before entering a recovery key, confirm your account (valid for 5 minutes). This way a sign-in redirect never clears your opened key or uses up an attempt.
step1.oauthOnlyHint: GitHub cannot prove fresh sign-in. Set a login password via verified email in Settings, or use Google if linked.

step2.title: Enter one recovery key
step2.lead: Paste a single unused key from your set of 10. Hyphens and uppercase/lowercase are normalized automatically.
step2.caption: Limited to 5 attempts per 15 minutes per account. Your key never leaves this browser — the server only receives a fingerprint of the key.

errors.invalidTitle: That recovery key is not valid.
errors.invalidBody: This single message is shown whether the key is malformed, unknown, already used, or belongs to another vault — without revealing how many keys remain. Check the characters or try another key from your set.
errors.rateLimitedTitle: Too many recovery attempts — please wait
errors.rateLimitedBody: Recovery key checks are limited to 5 per 15 minutes per account. Please wait {clock} ({seconds}s) before trying again. The server does not say how many attempts or recovery keys are left.
errors.aeadBadge: could not open · key not consumed
errors.aeadTitle: This recovery key could not open your vault
errors.aeadBody: The server found a match for this key, but your browser could not open the vault with it. This recovery key was not consumed — try again or use another key from your set of 10.
errors.networkBody: Check your connection and try again. Your recovery key was not consumed.

step3.title: Set a new passphrase to finish recovery.
step3.lead: Your recovery key opened the vault key in temporary memory. Set a new vault encryption passphrase (different from your login password) to finish — this step is required.
step3.recoveringNoteBody: The opened vault key is kept only to protect it with your new passphrase — entry contents cannot be opened and remember-device stays off until recovery completes. Leaving or cancelling now clears the key from memory and does not consume your recovery key.
step3.passphraseHint: Different from your account login password. At least 12 characters and hard to guess.
step3.footerNote: Only after this step succeeds is the recovery key deleted on the live server. Your remaining recovery keys (including old printouts), passkeys, and remembered devices keep working.

policyErrors.tooShort: Passphrase must be at least 12 characters.
policyErrors.tooWeak: Passphrase is too easy to guess. Add more uncommon words or characters until strength reaches Strong.
policyErrors.invalidUnicode: Passphrase contains invalid Unicode characters. Re-type your passphrase.

errors.reauthExpiredPasswordTitle: Re-authentication expired — confirm your login password in place
errors.reauthExpiredPasswordBody: Your account confirmation has less than 60 seconds left or has expired. Enter your account login password right here to confirm again without leaving this page — your opened key is kept.
errors.reauthExpiredOauthTitle: Time ran out — please start again
errors.reauthExpiredOauthBody: Confirming again with a sign-in provider needs a full-page redirect, which clears temporary memory. The opened key was cleared and your recovery key was NOT consumed — start again from step 1 to confirm your account and reuse the same key.
errors.oomTitle: Not enough memory to derive the new passphrase key
errors.oomBody: This browser could not set aside the 64 MiB of memory needed to derive a key from your new passphrase. Your recovery key has not been consumed. Close other tabs and retry, or complete recovery on another device.
errors.versionMismatchTitle: Vault was updated in another tab or device
errors.versionMismatchBody: The vault version on the server changed before recovery completed. Nothing from this tab was saved, and your recovery key was not consumed. Reload the latest vault state and start this step again.
errors.preconditionBody: Reload the latest vault state and try again.
errors.idempotencyInProgressTitle: Recovery completion is still in progress
errors.idempotencyInProgressBody: The previous request is still being processed. Wait a moment and retry with the same request key.
errors.idempotencyConflictBody: The request payload changed for the current idempotency key. Reload vault metadata and start again.
errors.mutationsDisabledTitle: Vault key changes are temporarily paused
errors.mutationsDisabledBody: Completing recovery is temporarily disabled for maintenance. Your recovery key was not consumed.
errors.rateLimitedTitle: Too many recovery completion requests — please wait
errors.rateLimitedBody: Finishing recovery is limited to 5 requests per 15 minutes (counted separately from key checks). Please wait {clock} ({seconds}s) before retrying.
errors.networkBody: Your connection dropped before the server confirmed completion. Retry safely — we reuse the exact same Idempotency-Key and request payload.
errors.completedWhileLockedTitle: Recovery completed — unlock with your new passphrase
errors.completedWhileLockedBody: Your new passphrase was saved on the server while this tab locked. Redirecting to unlock with your new passphrase…

step4Reauth.unlockedBanner: Vault unlocked. {remaining} of 10 recovery keys remain active ({emptySlots} empty after being consumed and deleted on the live server).
step4Reauth.allFullBanner: Vault unlocked. All 10 of 10 recovery keys are active.
step4Reauth.title: Re-authenticate before generating replacement keys
step4Reauth.lead: Generating replacement recovery keys for empty slots requires confirming your account at the start of this step — new keys are generated and shown only after re-authentication.
step4Reauth.cardBadge: Confirm your account before creating replacement keys
step4Reauth.cardBody: Creating replacement keys needs its own account confirmation (separate from the one used for recovery) before new keys are created for empty slots.
step4Reauth.googleCaption: Google re-authentication leaves the page: the vault locks again — unlock with the new passphrase (or a passkey) before replacement keys are generated.
step4Reauth.skipCaption: You can skip this step and keep {remaining} active keys, or regenerate missing slots anytime in Settings › Security.

wakeGate.title: Checking that your vault is still unlocked…
wakeGate.body: Replacement keys stay hidden and password entry is paused until this check finishes. Your recovery progress is kept.

committedRecheck.verifyingBody: Your new passphrase was saved on the server. We are confirming that your vault is still the one you recovered. Do not reuse the recovery key you just entered.
committedRecheck.recheckTitle: Recovery completed — we could not confirm it yet
committedRecheck.recheckBody: Your new passphrase was saved on the server and the recovery key you entered is used up, but we could not reach the server to confirm the current state of your vault. Check again, or unlock with your new passphrase.

step4.unlockedBanner: Vault unlocked. {remaining} of 10 recovery keys remain active (slots: {emptySlots}).
step4.title: Generate replacement keys for empty slots
step4.lead: Replacement keys are generated only for empty slots (lowest slot number first, 1…10). Your remaining {remaining} recovery keys and their existing printouts keep working and are not shown again.
step4.newKeyCaption: New key(s) for empty slot(s) {emptySlots} (shown only once):
step4.screenshotWarningBody: Print or download the replacement key(s) and store them alongside your existing recovery keys.
step4.gridLabel: Replacement recovery keys for empty slots
step4.copiedStatus: Copied replacement key(s) · clipboard clears in 30 seconds
step4.confirmSavedLabel: I have saved the replacement recovery key(s) ({emptySlots}) alongside my other {remaining} recovery keys.

errors.versionMismatchBody: Reload vault state and regenerate empty slots again.
errors.slotTakenBody: One of the empty slots was already regenerated in another tab or device. Reload recovery key status.
errors.reauthExpiredPasswordTitle: Re-authentication expired — confirm your login password in place
errors.networkBody: Retry safely with the same request key.

errors.hint_invalid: Item hint must be at most 120 characters and contain no control characters.
errors.tag_display_invalid: Tag name must be 1–50 characters and contain no control characters.
errors.item_id_conflict: This item ID is already in use by another item.
errors.item_deleted: This item was deleted. Restore the item first before restoring its entry.
errors.item_tag_limit: An item can have at most 20 active tags.
errors.item_entry_limit: An item can hold at most 200 active entries.
errors.tag_conflict: A tag with this normalized name already exists.
errors.entry_invalid: The entry envelope or encrypted payload is invalid.
errors.entry_too_large: An entry can be at most 256 KiB. Split it into smaller entries.
errors.entry_id_conflict: This entry ID is already in use.
errors.entry_key_mismatch: This entry was encrypted with an older vault key. Reload your vault state.
errors.entry_nonce_reused: Encryption nonce cannot be reused. Please save again to generate a fresh nonce.
errors.entry_restore_via_item: This entry was deleted along with its item. Restore the item instead.
errors.reorder_mismatch: The entry list changed on another device. Reloading the latest order.
errors.changes_window_expired: Sync history expired after 29 days. Reloading the full list.
errors.not_found: This item, tag, or entry was deleted or does not belong to your account.
errors.invalid_request: The request is invalid. Please check your input and try again.
errors.rate_limited: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again — your save will not be duplicated.
errors.precondition_required: Missing version precondition. Reload the latest version and try again.
errors.version_mismatch: This was edited on another device. Load the latest version or keep your draft.
errors.idempotency_conflict: Request key conflict with different payload. Please start the action again.
errors.idempotency_in_progress: Your previous save is still being processed. Retrying shortly with the same key.
errors.vault_absent: Your vault has not been set up or was reset. Set up your vault before saving entries.
errors.dependency_unavailable: The server is temporarily busy. Your draft is safe — please retry.
errors.unauthenticated: Your session has ended. Sign in again to continue.
errors.access_expired: Your session expired and could not be refreshed automatically. Your draft is safe — please retry.

errors.offline: You are offline. Cannot save right now — your draft stays in this input until the vault locks.

entry.networkFailedBody: Could not reach the server to download this entry. Check your connection and try again.
entry.notFoundBody: This entry was deleted or is no longer available in your account.

entry.oldKeyTitle: This entry was encrypted with an older vault key
entry.oldKeyBody: The encryption key on this entry does not match your current vault key, so decryption was skipped. This happens after a vault reset or key change on another device.

entry.singleInFlightHint: Only one in-flight save per entry at a time.
entry.saveFailedRetryBody: Connection dropped before confirmation. Your draft stays in memory until the vault locks — click Retry to resend the exact sealed payload and idempotency key without duplicating data.
entry.discardConfirmBody: Your edits in this entry have not been saved.
entry.mixedEolWarning: This document has mixed line endings; saving from this editor will convert line endings to {target}.
entry.conflictBody: A newer version exists on the server. We never overwrite automatically. Load the latest version, keep your version (re-seal with a fresh nonce and overwrite intentionally), or copy your draft to merge manually.
entry.reloadConfirmPrompt: Discard your draft and load the latest server version?
entry.deletedRemotelyTitle: This entry was deleted on another device
entry.deletedRemotelyBody: Your draft is still kept here. You can save it as a new entry.
entry.draftClearedOnLock: Unsaved draft was cleared when the vault locked
entry.saveUnconfirmed: Previous save in {name} was not confirmed; check the item before saving again
